accept.reason: the file holds the two index paths from before .claudinite/flat/ (#2322) as the one place the engine spells them: converge removes an old index it finds there and rewrites the CLAUDE.md import naming it, so the paths must not resolve to a file in the canon and every member still carrying one must keep being recognised. Collected here so this waiver is one entry, the tests reading them from it; #2323 retires the tolerance

the update worker has a SECOND, deliberate caller: .github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml drives it directly to qualify a release ref, and CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF is that harness's own parameter, set there and read nowhere else. The rule's concern is a parameter channel that has silently stopped being delivered; this one is delivered by the workflow beside it, in the same repo, and its absence under code-work is the normal case the worker already handles (rehearsalRef null = a real cycle)

the file holds the LEGACY WIRE LITERALS, which are data rather than pointers: a work item minted before the task surface moved (#1317) still carries `engine/scheduler/` in its machine block, and `BUILT_IN_PATH_RE` accepts that root permanently because it is a validator — dropping it rejects that half of the ad-hoc request lane outright. The path must not resolve to a file; a decoder must keep understanding it. Collected here so this waiver is one entry rather than five across the tests that exercise the decode

the live canary gate names packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update because the worker is ITSELF vendored content, so a release that changes the worker cannot be rehearsed by the canary's vendored copy — that copy predates the release by definition, and a rehearsal driving it would ignore CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF entirely and run a real cycle against main, opening a PR on the canary instead of qualifying the ref. The crossing buys the one property the gate exists for: the code under test is the code every member runs the moment the release reaches them. The workflow names no pack CONTENT — only the entry point of the task that performs the converge

every task's work step moved from a `code_work` command to a `code_worker_mjs` module, so the 17 workers that exported `main` as their entry point now export `worker` instead. None of the three discharges fits. A task's worker is spawned BY PATH and never imported, and the old `main` took no arguments and read the whole code-work environment, so it is unusable outside the subprocess the executor starts: no member can hold a consumer of that name, which is what the rule's harm (a local pack failing to load and wedging the converge) requires. A re-export shim would keep the name resolvable while giving it an incompatible signature, trading a loud load-time error for a quiet runtime one. A rehearsal fixture cannot prove anything about a name that is gone. A migration record would spend an agent session in every member converging to a no-op. Owner's call, taken in session on 2026-09-22 with all three alternatives on the table
